text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem co-chairman of Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, says he believes that the donnors' conference scheduled for June 24-25 will be postponed until July 12 after Serb leaders failed to approve legislation on customs and tariffs.

- Diplomatic sources say that the United States is proposing to replace outgoing deputy High Representative to Bosnia, Michael Steiner, with the U.N. envoy in Croatia's Eastern Slavonia region, Jacques Klein, or diplomat William Walker.

- Meeting between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and chairman of Bosnian presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, will not be held next week in Split as previously reported. They could meet by the end of June if problem of forming joint police force in southwest Neretva canton is solved.
- Trial of two French citizens accused of killing a Bosnian policeman has been postponed until July 7.
- The only solution to present problems in Bosnia is full implementation of the Dayton peace agreement, says new High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp.
- U.S. Agency for International Develoment (USAID) signed a memorandum of understanding with officials from the town of Brcko, pledging 3.7 million dollars to fund repair of infrastructure.

- Representatives of Bosnia's Serb and Moslem-Croat entities agreed that joint military doctrines of the two entities will call for protecting the sovereignity and the territorial integrity of the state and that military force will not be used used to resolve outstanding issues.
- NATO-led Stabilisation Force confiscated several heavy weapons on Wednesday near Omarska in the Serb entity and at a Bosnian federation army weapons site in Litnica, SFOR says.
